measurementNotes: Only the gate implementation translation unit is compiled with -msimd128 in the candidate. SoundEffects.o and all strict floating-point flags are identical; no SSE, fast-math, Huffman change, new resampler or PCM backend.

Each operation is timed by host performance.now around one synchronous Wasm call. A/B order alternates per operation type, so repeated read/clamp pairs do not fix one instance first for every read. Setup, PCM buffer clearing, queries, comparison and hashing occur outside read/mix timers. Open, command, seek, clamp and close have separate samples.
All raw elapsed samples remain, including cold module initialization, first reads, decoder opens and warm reads. No performance threshold, outlier removal or CPU-throttle inference.

PCM is compared byte for byte before and after the same in-place clamp. Public decoder/sound status, length, cursor, format, playing/looping, gain/pan/pitch, engine time and every SoundEffects queue element are serialized without pointers and compared. No PCM output files are stored.

Source stream EOF and hot seek0/odd/nonzero seek retain existing miniaudio resampler/filter history, including any baseline quirks. Two independent actual decoders are compared, never a cold PCM substitute.

OGG uses the same file pull decoder as AudioDevice, frame-length validation and intro/end loop points. Music-only and 54-SFX-plus-music engines keep original 44100 stereo no-pitch/no-spatialization configuration.

Node WASI compiler/runtime differs from Emscripten/browser. Passing this component gate is necessary evidence, not a substitute for production build feature inspection and subsequent live/release acceptance.
Host competition is not isolated in this component runner. Microsecond-scale Node elapsed pairs do not establish a 4x live improvement.
This fixed workload is not a proof for all malformed assets, NaN inputs, device configurations, or all possible command sequences. Stereo/mono WAV rate and seek boundaries use actual fixtures.
This evidence is an offline aggregation; no new compilation, browser or audio workload was run during review.
79,883,284 float comparisons count both before and after clamp and count requested buffers, including zero tails. They are not unique source samples or a new PCM cache allocation.

Per-case timing combines separate calls and is diagnostic elapsed time. All cold init/open/first-read, warm, seek/control and close samples remain. Positive simdMinusScalar is worse; no thresholds filter samples.

The target_features section and compiler vectorization remarks confirm this gate candidate was compiled with SIMD. Remarks may include inlined copies or unused APIs; they are not a count of executed SIMD instructions.

Standard SIMD was only requested for the implementation TU, SoundEffects.o and link flags stayed scalar. Compiler/code layout and runtime effects can still affect elapsed times; production Emscripten/Binaryen validation is separate.
The gate omits SDL's queue/refill/playback device and output-rate conversion, network confirmation publication, scheduling, live Draw and rAF. It cannot explain or resolve a multi-second rAF gap.
Node/WASI host competition and first/second file-cache effects are not isolated. Per-export alternating order is verified; no inference of browser CPU-throttle gain is made.
WebAssembly.Module construction is outside the module instantiateAndInitializeMs field; the entire gateWall includes construction as well as compilation and all work.

timing.units: milliseconds; synchronous host elapsed around one Wasm export
timing.deltaDefinition: SIMD minus scalar; positive is slower
